answer: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The defence rests on woodturner guild membership with lathe work records: turned pieces logged at one workshop for years. The price is per head, and the dune test proves it: Forging 124 of these means building 124 separate work records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The mesa trail is public, the haven check is cheap to run, and a farm of 124 aliases pays 124 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
